event_check: The IPO priced 2026-04-15 and its final prospectus is dated then (424B4 filed 2026-04-17, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000119312526160250/0001193125-26-160250-index.htm). I could not open the main 424B4 document (over 10 MB), so the 180-day term is confirmed from a secondary source: syndicated MarketBeat coverage dated 2026-10-12 (https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8944583) gives the expiry as Tuesday 2026-10-13, which matches Nasdaq's date. EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002098430&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40): no filing after 2026-08-27, no 8-K amending the lock-up, no follow-on prospectus, no waiver, no Form 144. The full-text probe for 'early release' returns 0 hits. The 2026-08-25 PIPE was a private placement and put no new lock-up on the IPO-locked holders (8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000162828026058764/mair-20260825.htm). So today is the first free session for the holders bound only by the 180-day underwriter lock-up. It is NOT a release for the controller's Class B stock or the Bertarelli entities. Both signed separate lock-ups with the company that run two years from the prospectus date (ex10_5 and ex10_6 to the 2026-04-17 8-K).
lockup_status: full expiry today of the 180-day underwriter lock-up, but that covers only the remainder: roughly 37M Class A (Madison Air Co-Investors LLC 12.3M plus about 24.7M held by IAQ Holdings II investors and Madison IAS executives, employees and consultants). The 324.4M Class B shares (Madison Industries Holdings) and 44.8M Class A held by K.C. Armada and Kedge (Bertarelli) stay locked to about April 2028 under company lock-ups. The 2026-09-01 PIPE shares (90.1M) are unregistered; the Gies parts are locked one year.
conviction_note: The freeable supply is small next to the headline: about 37M of 501M shares, around 16 days of the 2.3M-share daily volume, and part of it sits with the controller's own vehicle. Short interest was built into the date: 10.3M shares at 9/30, up 30%. Together these give a small positive lean on top of the flat-to-up lock-up base rate (55% up). I put p_up at 55 on a 2.0% scale, near this name's 1.82% open-to-close sd. The findings sum to +0.45 against the scaled +0.2. Both are small and agree in sign; the gap is the employee-seller finding, which pulls the scaled number toward 50.
bar: This name's own 20-session open-to-close sd of 1.82% (median absolute 1.11%), from baseline.tape. The phase-0 lock-up base rate is median +0.32%, median absolute 2.78%, 55% up, from baseline.phase0.lockup. The below-offer bucket is median +0.19%, 54% up.
positioning_check: Short interest: 10.3M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 30.4% from 7.9M on 9/15, days to cover 4.1. It peaked at 12.3M on 6/30. Borrow fee 0.4% on the 10/12 close, with about 4.3-4.6M shares available. Source: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mair/ (updated 2026-10-13). FINRA publishes about 8 business days after settlement, so the 10/15 settlement cannot be seen. Form 144: none on EDGAR through the 2026-10-14 cut. Insiders: the controller (Gies) bought 24.8M PIPE shares at $24.97 on 2026-08-25 (Form 4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000119312526371628/xslF345X06/ownership.xml). Director La Force bought 20,000 shares at $27.84 the same day. Baseline insider summary: 3 open-market buys and 1 sell in 3 months. Baseline tape: spot $24.08, 10.8% below the $27 offer, 5-day run-in -2.1%, 20-day +0.75%, 5-day volume 0.83x the 20-day.

findings.finding: Only about 37M Class A shares can come free today: roughly 7% of the 501M total shares, or about 16 days of the ~2.3M-share daily volume ($55.5M/day 20-day turnover at $24). That is far smaller than the 'shares held by major shareholders and insiders become tradable' framing in the syndicated coverage. The 324.4M Class B shares (Madison Industries Holdings, 64.7% economic) and the 44.8M Class A held by Bertarelli's K.C. Armada (37.6M before the PIPE) and Kedge (7.2M) are under separate company lock-ups to two years after the 2026-04-15 prospectus. Arithmetic: 176.9M Class A on 2026-04-17, minus 95.1M IPO shares including the full greenshoe, leaves 81.8M non-IPO Class A; minus 44.8M two-year-locked gives about 37M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Phase-0: lock-ups with smaller locked shares (<70% locked) had median +0.19% open-to-close, 58% up. The release here is far smaller than the bucket the baseline's 50% float share suggests. No dated source on two-year-controller-lock structures.
findings.why_not_priced: The public framing, the MarketBeat syndications of 2026-10-12, gives only the 82.7M IPO size and 501M shares outstanding and says insiders' shares become tradable. The two-year locks are in 8-K exhibits and the Bertarelli Form 4, not in the coverage. If the open fully held the small real supply, there would be no pre-date drift. The stock fell 2.1% over the 5-day run-in into the date and short interest rose 30% into 9/30, which looks like positioning for a larger unlock than the documents allow.
findings.independence: The Bertarelli Form 4 (2026-08-27) gives K.C. Armada 46,387,522 shares after buying 8,770,524 in the PIPE, and Kedge 7,224,073: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000119312526371312/xslF345X06/ownership.xml. The Kedge two-year lock-up is at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000119312526161509/ck0002098430-ex10_6.htm. Class counts are from the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002098430/000162828026033863/mair-20260331.htm.

findings.finding: Of the ~37M freed shares, 12.3M (2.5% of Class A) sit in Madison Air Co-Investors LLC, which files jointly with Larry Gies and Madison Industries in their 13G (event date 2026-06-30). Gies bought 24.8M shares at $24.97 in the 2026-08-25 PIPE and committed up to EUR 1.3bn of backstop equity for ebm-papst, so this third of the free supply sits with a holder who is buying, not selling. Affiliate sales also fall under Rule 144 volume limits, and no Form 144 is on EDGAR.
findings.why_not_priced: Co-Investors' place in the free supply only shows when the 13G is read against the share count; no coverage of the unlock mentions it. If it were priced, the unlock would be treated as about 25M of genuinely saleable shares, not 37M or the headline. This is a small refinement, and the open may already hold some of it.
findings.independence: The 10-Q says IAQ Holdings III investors contributed their Class A to Co-Investors LLC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002098430/000162828026033863/mair-20260331.htm. Gies's PIPE purchase Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000119312526371628/xslF345X06/ownership.xml

findings.finding: The rest of the freed supply, about 24.7M Class A by subtraction, belongs to IAQ Holdings II investors and to 'certain executive officers and other current and former employees and consultants' (Madison IAS Investors), whose interests converted into Class A in the organizational transactions. Their basis is far below the $24.08 spot even though the stock is 10.8% under the $27 offer. Former employees and consultants are the most likely day-one sellers, against about 2.3M shares of daily volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Phase-0: over 137 lock-ups the first free session was median +0.32%, 55% up, and volume ran about 1.35x average. Employee supply has, on that sample, mostly been met by buyers. none found specific to employee-rollover holders.
findings.why_not_priced: The open prices the expected overhang, but how fast a dispersed employee and consultant base sells only shows once orders arrive in the session. A heavier-than-expected tape after the open would take the price below it. If this were fully priced, the session would trade on the open with ordinary volume. The holder counts are not public, so this is an inference from the 10-Q's holder description and the share arithmetic.
findings.independence: S-8 on file since 2026-04-17 (EAR plan shares registered for resale); an officer's Form 4 shows EAR units vesting and shares withheld (Leah Larson, 2026-08-21): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2098430/000162828026058831/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1787682959.xml

findings.finding: Short interest rose into the date: 10.3M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 30.4% from 7.9M on 9/15, with 4.1 days to cover and a cheap 0.4% borrow. That is roughly 11% of the ~95M IPO Class A float that was tradable before the unlock. Shorts positioned for an unlock that, by the documents, releases a small and partly controller-held block may cover into the session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Phase-0: open-to-close of the first free session is flat to up (median +0.32%, net of IWM +0.73%, 62% up), which is consistent with pre-positioned selling being done before the open. none found specific to MAIR.
findings.why_not_priced: The open reflects the overnight book. Covering by shorts who sold for the date tends to come during the session, once the unlock's volume turns out lighter than feared. If the shorts had already covered, the 10/15 settlement would show it, and that cannot be seen today. Part of the rise may be institutional PIPE buyers hedging their unregistered $24.97 shares. Those shorts would not cover today, so I sized this small.
findings.independence: The syndicated MarketBeat lock-up articles of 2026-10-12 put the date in front of every retail screen (https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8944583). The baseline tape shows a 5-day run-in of -2.1% into the date.

findings.finding: The controller and a director bought at or above spot: Gies bought 24.8M shares at $24.97 in the PIPE that closed about 2026-09-01, and director La Force bought 20,000 shares at $27.84 on 2026-08-25. Spot is $24.08, 3.6% below the PIPE price and 10.8% below the $27 offer. The holders who could sell large blocks are buyers, which leaves no controller or sponsor block-sale risk today.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Phase-0 below-offer bucket: median +0.19%, 54% up (72 lock-ups).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the buying is seven weeks old and public. What it adds for today is that no sponsor-style block or overnight secondary is possible from the largest holders. A typical PE-backed unlock carries that risk and it shows up as a discount at the open. This one should not.

outside_window.finding: Resale registration for the ~65M institutional PIPE shares sold at $24.97 (90.1M total less Gies's 24.8M, which is locked one year) must be filed within 90 days of the ~2026-09-01 closing, or up to 120 days if the ebm-papst financials are not ready. That makes the larger, real overhang due around late November to December 2026, and those holders are under water at $24.08.
Q3 2026 results: date not yet announced. Q1 and Q2 calls were each announced about two weeks ahead, so this is likely late October or early November.
ebm-papst acquisition (EUR 4.775bn EV) expected to close 2026-12-31, subject to merger-control, FDI and EU FSR clearances; EUR 250m break fee.

baseline_tension: Consistent with the base rates: the documents show a small, partly controller-held release on a name with short interest built into the date, which fits the flat-to-slightly-up lock-up session. The baseline's 50% float share overstates how much is released today, because most of the remainder is under two-year company lock-ups.
